doc: MiaMe.co.il — the migration phase manifest.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Code deployed to Vercel lands IMMEDIATELY; a migration
lands only when a human runs an approved apply. That asymmetry is the whole
reason a phase model is needed: without one, a reader ships before the column
it reads exists, and the site answers 500 until someone notices.
A PHASE IS ONE APPROVED UNIT OF WORK. One phase per apply run. A phase that
has landed moves to status 'applied' and drops out of the pending menu — a
phase left in the menu after it landed makes the live plan and the approved
plan diverge, and the next run aborts on a plan it cannot reconcile.
THE THREE STATUSES ARE NOT COSMETIC:
applied — present in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations on the MiaMe
project. 'ledger' records the version string production actually
carries, which is NOT always the repo filename prefix.
pending — a real MiaMe migration that has never landed. Eligible to apply.
foreign — written against the SHARED leasing-co-il-prod database, not the
MiaMe data plane. NEVER applied here. See 'why' on each entry.
The 'foreign' status is the finding this file was built to carry. The MiaMe
project holds exactly six tables (events · knowledge · leads · partners ·
vehicle_media_assets · vehicle_media_events). Three files in this directory
address catalog_2026 tables and seo/catalog trigger functions that do not
exist here and never will — they were authored while MiaMe and the leasing
platform shared one database. Applying them against MiaMe does not degrade
anything; it ABORTS, because ALTER FUNCTION on an absent function throws.
Marking them keeps them reviewable without leaving them armed.

phases.title: Reconcile knowledge columns with the repo declaration
phases.risk: none — additive, idempotent, no live consumer branches on either column
why: Measured drift, both directions. Production carries `category` and no
migration in this repo creates it — so a replay onto a fresh database
ABORTS at the 20260714 seed, which INSERTs into that column. The repo
declares `updated_at` and production does not have it.
Lands first because every later phase assumes the table matches the repo.

phases.title: Consolidate the vehicle_media_assets policy set
phases.risk: low — policy replacement on a table with no anon write path
why: Measured 2026-08-31: vehicle_media_assets carries 2 policies; this file
declares 4. Review against 20260723115108 (already applied) BEFORE the
apply — that later file also rewrote this policy set, and the winner
must be decided by reading, not by apply order.

phases.title: UTM attribution columns on leads
phases.risk: low — additive columns on an existing table
why: Measured 2026-08-31: public.leads exists and carries ZERO utm columns.
Genuine MiaMe work that never landed. The campaign now drives paid
traffic into nine WhatsApp entry points, so attribution has a consumer.

phases.title: Rental fleet OS — four tables
why: Measured 2026-08-31: none of the four tables exist.
HOLD. The focused sales campaign removed the rental surface from the
site, so this schema currently has no reader. Landing it would create
four empty tables nobody queries. Apply only if rental returns as a
product decision — not as migration housekeeping.

phases.title: Full knowledge corpus seed (replay path only)
phases.risk: none on production — ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, and all 29 ids already exist
why: Inert against the live database by construction. It matters for REPLAY:
on a fresh database this is what fills the corpus before the campaign
alignment runs.
Its three campaign-sensitive rows were aligned at source on 2026-08-31
so the file is correct in isolation, not only after a later patch.

phases.title: catalog_2026 RLS hardening — SHARED LEASING DATABASE
why: Targets leads_2026 · deals_2026 · catalog_audit_log_2026 ·
vehicle_inventory_units_2026 · zero_km_disclosures_2026 ·
catalog_health_snapshots_2026. NONE of them exist on the MiaMe project
(six tables measured 2026-08-31). The file says so itself in its header:
its target is leasing-co-il-prod.
Kept in git as a reviewable artifact. Never applied here.

phases.title: Pin search_path on seo/catalog trigger fns — SHARED LEASING DATABASE
why: ALTERs public.seo_touch_updated_at() and public.catalog_touch_updated_at().
Measured 2026-08-31 on the MiaMe project: NEITHER function exists, so the
bare ALTER does not degrade — it THROWS, and takes the transaction with it.
Guarded at source on 2026-08-31 so a replay cannot abort on it, but the
status stays foreign: the functions belong to the leasing data plane.

phases.title: SPYQE knowledge rows + MIA FOUR's real supply commitment
phases.risk: low — six additive rows plus two id-keyed UPDATEs on rows that are now factually wrong
why: Two models now, two different waits: MIA FOUR is in stock and ships in up to
3 business days; SPYQE is a pre-order estimated at up to 33. The corpus knew
about neither, so a SPYQE question was answered out of MIA FOUR's rows.
Every embedding is NULL, so retrieval runs entirely on the Hebrew keyword
fallback — and every existing spec-*/price-* row describes MIA FOUR without
saying so. That is why each new row NAMES its model inside the body text and
not only in the id: the keyword path matches the body, so a model name that
lives only in the id is invisible to it.
`spyqe-spec` carries no specification on purpose. It exists so the assistant
has something correct to say when asked for one, instead of reaching for
MIA FOUR's numbers.
The offer text lives in this row AND in lib/spyqe.ts. That duplication is
real and deliberate — the corpus is a database, not an import of the bundle —
so when the 248 allocation closes or the price moves, BOTH must be updated.
The rollback restores the previous `delivery` body verbatim.
`lead` still quotes a balloon payment; the simulator has none (balloonPct is pinned to 0).
